title: Integrality of the normalized stratum polynomials
statement:
In the situation of [prop-galois-weight-strata], for every integer
$i$ with $0\leq i\leq2d$ the normalized stratum polynomial

$$
Q_i(T)=\prod_{\alpha\in R_i}(1-\alpha T)
$$

over the $q$-Weil numbers of weight $i$
lies in $\mathbf Z[T]$.

proof.text: Fix $0\le i\le2d$ and put $C=A$ for odd $i$, $C=B$ for even $i$, using the data and the submultiset $R_i$ of [prop-galois-weight-strata]. Thus $C\in\mathbf Z[T]$ and $C(0)=1$. Put $r=\deg C$ and write $C=\sum_{j=0}^{r}c_jT^j$, so $c_0=1$ and $c_r\ne0$. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-reciprocal-polynomial] gives the monic integer polynomial $C^\#(U)=\sum_{j=0}^r c_jU^{r-j}$. Every $\alpha$ in $R_i$ is a root of this polynomial by the specified definition of $R_i$. Hence every such $\alpha$ is an algebraic integer by [def-weil-algebraic-integer]. If $r=0$, then $C=C^\#=1$ and $R_i$ is empty, so the assertion about its elements is vacuous.

source.place: First sentence: reciprocal polynomials are monic with integer coefficients

proof.text: Apply [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] to $\mathbf Z\to\overline{\mathbf Q}$. Its statement says that the elements integral over $\mathbf Z$ form a subring $S$ containing the integers. Step 1 puts every occurrence $\alpha$ of $R_i$ in $S$, so the coefficients $1,-\alpha$ of each $1-\alpha T$ lie in $S$. To verify the same for their product without assuming a symmetric-function theorem, enumerate the occurrences as $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_N$ and set $H_0=1$, $H_{m+1}=H_m(1-\alpha_{m+1}T)$. By the convolution definition in [def-weil-polynomial-ring], $[T^n]H_{m+1}=[T^n]H_m-\alpha_{m+1}[T^{n-1}]H_m$ for $n\ge1$, and the constant coefficient is unchanged. Induction on $m$, using the subring operations, puts every coefficient of $H_N=Q_i$ in $S$. It also shows $Q_i(0)=1$ and $\deg Q_i\le N$. This treats multiplicities as separate occurrences and includes $N=0$.

source.place: First paragraph: elementary symmetric functions and coefficients are algebraic integers

proof.text:
For every $\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(\overline{\mathbf Q}/\mathbf Q)$, [prop-galois-weight-strata] gives equality of multisets $\sigma(R_i)=R_i$, including multiplicities. The coefficientwise ring homomorphism of [def-weil-coefficientwise-ring-hom-map] fixes $T$, sends $1-\alpha T$ to $1-\sigma(\alpha)T$, and preserves finite products. Consequently
$$
\sigma(Q_i)=\prod_{\alpha\in R_i}(1-\sigma(\alpha)T)=\prod_{\beta\in\sigma(R_i)}(1-\beta T)=Q_i.
$$
The middle equality merely reindexes the same finite list of occurrences; the final equality uses the equality of multisets. Comparing the coefficient of $T^n$ yields $\sigma([T^n]Q_i)=[T^n]Q_i$ for every $n$.

source.place: Last paragraph: coefficients fixed by Gal(Qbar/Q)

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-algebraic-closure-fixed-rational] to $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}$ and $x=[T^n]Q_i$. The field here is precisely the algebraic closure of $\mathbf Q$ in the hypotheses of [prop-galois-weight-strata], and Step 3 verifies invariance under every $\mathbf Q$-automorphism, not just one chosen embedding. Thus each coefficient is the image of some rational number. Step 2 says the same coefficient is integral over $\mathbf Z$, so [lem-weil-rational-algebraic-integer] makes it the image of an integer $z_n$. Choose these integers for $0\le n\le N$ and set $P(T)=\sum_{n=0}^{N}z_nT^n\in\mathbf Z[T]$. Above degree $N$ both its image and $Q_i$ have zero coefficients by Step 2, and at the remaining degrees their coefficients agree by construction. Hence the image of $P$ in $\overline{\mathbf Q}[T]$ is $Q_i$, which is exactly $Q_i\in\mathbf Z[T]$.

source.place: Last paragraph: rational coefficients and rational algebraic integers are integers

This follows sk-thm-intfactors point (ii), retaining point (i) Galois stability as a dependency.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q145-a7fe86231 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, both new nodes and every cited statement. The item statement matches the main-20261015 and master blueprint statements exactly, and steps 1-4 follow the four moves of the main-20261015 proof. Step 1: clause (1) of lem-weil-reciprocal-polynomial (c_0=1, c_r!=0, R=Z) gives a monic C^# with integer coefficients, so the roots in R_i are algebraic integers; when r=0, R_i is empty and the claim is vacuous. Step 2 is correctly marked elementary: the integral elements form a subring (def-weil-pbc-integral-closure), and an induction on the polynomial-ring convolution puts every coefficient of Q_i in it. Step 3 uses the with-multiplicities Galois stability of R_i from prop-galois-weight-strata and the coefficientwise ring homomorphism, which fixes T. Step 4 uses the two leaves and builds P in Z[T] explicitly. The leaves are verified in local Mathlib: InfiniteGalois.mem_range_algebraMap_iff_fixed at Infinite.lean:114-116, with IsGalois inferred through PerfectField.ofCharZero (Perfect.lean:306), IsSepClosure.of_isAlgClosure_of_perfectField (IsSepClosed.lean:251) and IsSepClosure.isGalois (IsSepClosed.lean:267); and IsIntegral.exists_int_iff_exists_rat at Niven.lean:34-39.
